course: Well, I think this course was arranged neatly and it was the only course I found helpful and educative this semester. I, however, think that there can be improvements regarding the content: first of all, I think there should be a change regarding the reading list content. We, for example, read Said and Spivak in the early weeks of the course, then moved onto Moretti, then we read articles in the last weeks which draw mostly on Said and Spivak’s arguments. I think this arrangement of the texts make it a little confusing for the students to understand the development and the changes in the theory. Secondly, I think the literary works are spread in reading list heterogeneously.  This  made  it hard for everyone to remember,  for example, Borges from the early weeks when we reached to the last quarter of the course. I think turning to the classical theory-class format would solve this problem. By that I mean, if a novel or another form of literary work, which would lend itself to interpretation based on the theories we read, was chosen for this course, it would make it easier for everyone to remember the original text. Last of all,  I think the presentations in the course could be shorter or cut off totally; this would create more space for in-group and in-class discussions. I know that the presentations  are used as a sort of introductory content but they were summarizing the texts sometimes and the summaries made it hard for me to follow the slide shows. I am aware that not everyone read the texts and they should be somehow made aware of what is going on but if they are taking this course, they should read the text in the question. Wow! I have written a longish feedback but just don’t take me wrong—it is not to be mean or to criticize this course totally. As said before, I really enjoyed this course and I want everyone to enjoy it after me— the above are just the elements that would, I think, make this course stronger.
